subject: Control/Data Plane split and egress pattern review — EdgeCloud private deployment
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@edgecloud.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: eng@edgecloud.com
Date: 2028-06-10T09:15:00Z
Subject: Planning review: split control/data plane and outbound egress patterns

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for taking the time. We want to validate the architecture for our upcoming private deployment of Redwood in our US region. High level ask: we need a short architecture review focused on the control vs data-plane split, how control-plane traffic will reach Redwood control endpoints, and recommended egress patterns for model telemetry + telemetry masking. A couple constraints:

- All customer inference traffic must stay on-prem; only orchestration/metrics may egress to Redwood control plane.
- Outbound egress must go through a central egress gateway that does TLS inspection and DLP.
- We require mutual TLS for the control plane, and a fallback path if that region is unreachable.

I attached our network sketch (edgecloud-deploy-diagram-v1.png) and a short list of compliance constraints. Can the Redwood team propose a pattern and call out operational risks?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Lead Infra Architect | EdgeCloud

--
Attachment: edgecloud-deploy-diagram-v1.png (image/png)
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@edgecloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-10T11:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Planning review: split control/data plane and outbound egress patterns

Rajiv — thanks, this is helpful. Quick readout from our side attached (edgecloud-deploy-diagram-v2.png) and an initial matrix (control-data-egress-matrix.xlsx). Key recommendations up-front:

1) Strict control/data separation: keep inference traffic (data plane) entirely within your VPCs and behind tenant-aware internal load balancers.
2) Control plane egress: allow a limited set of outbound flows from a small pool of management hosts through your central egress gateway to our control endpoints. These flows must be mTLS with client certs managed by your KMS/HSM.
3) Fallbacks: configure a regional second-hop to our backup control endpoint and set an exponential backoff on registration attempts.
4) Telemetry: send aggregated telemetry (metrics/traces) over a separate egress route with PII-stripping at the gateway. We recommend tokenized traces rather than full request payloads.

Operational risks:
- Misconfigured NAT or proxy that allows data-plane traffic to leak out.
- Certificate rotation processes that are not automated could cause control-plane outages.

Next steps: Can we schedule a 45min call to walk the diagram? I also called out a couple of decisions for your team: preferred egress IP ranges and whether DLP will perform content redaction or blocking.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Partner Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: edgecloud-deploy-diagram-v2.png (image/png); control-data-egress-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@edgecloud.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-10T14:25:00Z
Subject: RE: Planning review: split control/data plane and outbound egress patterns

Adding a few specifics from the runtime/ops perspective:

- Control plane hosts should be single-purpose and isolated from the data-plane GPU subnet. Use RBAC to limit who can request control-plane certs.
- For mTLS we prefer using short-lived certs (1 hour) issued by your internal CA; Redwood supports client cert rotation via ACME-like automation or API-driven rotation.
- BGP vs static routing for the egress gateway: BGP gives faster failover but is more operationally complex. If you have an SDN fabric, we recommend BGP with graceful restart.
- Lock down DNS for control endpoints and pin on-customer side TLS roots to prevent MITM during fallback.

I'll add notes to the matrix about suggested iptables rules and IDS signatures that our ops team usually deploys.

-Neha
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@edgecloud.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-11T09:40:00Z
Subject: RE: Planning review: split control/data plane and outbound egress patterns

Rajiv — quick question on service discovery and NAT hairpinning: in your diagram the inference nodes will reach a local load balancer for model-serving (no egress). For control-plane registration, do you expect the hosts to egress via the same NAT IP pool as admin tools, or will you allocate a dedicated egress pool for Redwood control traffic?

If it's shared, we'll recommend strict source-port tagging and firewall rules to ensure only the control-plane processes can reach our control endpoints (we can provide a short-lived token to validate). If it's dedicated, please provide the egress CIDR so we can whitelist.

Also recommending a small metrics relay (two replicas) inside your management VPC that aggregates and forwards metrics to reduce connection churn to our control plane.

Thanks,
Jonas
Runtime Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@edgecloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-11T12:07:00Z
Subject: RE: Planning review: split control/data plane and outbound egress patterns

Thanks Jonas — we will allocate a dedicated egress pool for Redwood control traffic. Egress CIDR: 198.51.100.0/27 (this will traverse our central DLP gateway). For metrics relay: we can run two small EC2- equivalent VMs in the management VPC; they will TLS-terminate to the gateway and forward aggregated payloads.

One follow-up: our security team asks whether Redwood supports partial telemetry redaction (strip request text before sending) and what SDK changes are required.

-Rajiv
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@edgecloud.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-12T16:04:00Z
Subject: RE: Planning review: split control/data plane and outbound egress patterns

Rajiv — quick confirmation and action items from Redwood security/runtime:

1) Telemetry redaction: yes, Redwood supports pre-send redaction hooks in the local SDK and the metrics relay idea is exactly the right pattern. We can provide a small shim that strips user request text and replaces it with a safe token before forwarding. That shim can be deployed as a sidecar or on the relay VMs.
2) Egress CIDR whitelist: we'll add 198.51.100.0/27 to our allowlist for control-plane registration and management APIs.
3) Cert rotation: we'll share our recommended automation scripts and an integration doc for your CA (action: irene to upload the script bundle).
4) Fallback routing: suggest a 30s connect timeout, exponential backoff with jitter up to 5 minutes, and local cache of the last-known-good control endpoint.

Action items:
- Rajiv: confirm whether DLP will redact or block payloads (needed to finalize the SDK shim behavior).
- Rajiv: confirm SLA for gateway egress availability and any maintenance windows.
- Irene: upload cert rotation scripts and the shim prototype to the shared drive by 2028-06-14.

I'll schedule a 45min call for early next week to walk through the diagram and finalize the matrix.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
